# the contributor audit: fixed face witnesses and circuit kernels

Source: `candidate 4a38a3cfd6733dce`, Sections 1--8, including the emerging-base revision of 2026-09-25.

**PASS with the stated full mixed-volume and signed-linearity scopes.** No OC constant follows merely from this result.

The minimal face of a strict midpoint is the join of the two endpoint minimal faces. For two different inclusion-maximal occupied faces, their witnesses therefore cannot share a parity: the integer midpoint would occupy a strictly larger face. This proves a fixed face cover with at most the occupied parity count; it is independent of circuit choices and permits overlapping faces.

The deepest-base set is lattice-complete because the ambient depth superlevel is convex and the convex combination of actual deepest points at an integer base still belongs to C intersect Lambda. Compactness and upper semicontinuity give an attained positive maximum. Positive-volume bases are themselves lattice-complete, and zero-volume bases outside their hull have a zero-mass pure-integer separating cap.

A positive-depth point is interior to its positive fiber: in the canonical face body a boundary support has a nonzero continuous component, and an added exposing base functional excludes every other base. Its supporting cap has zero mixed measure. Consequently any critical nonvertical cap through a deepest point has a proper own section. A deepest point cannot lie strictly inside that cap, since shifting the threshold would remove a positive own-fiber strip and give a smaller containing cap.

Positive balancing of the continuous circuit normals projects this contact to a supporting inequality of the deepest-base hull. The equality face contains the anchor's minimal face, and the original closed caps cover the whole continuous plane above every base in that face. This verifies oblique as well as vertical-base components exactly.

The quantile adjustment keeps all original normals and the weighted threshold sum fixed. It therefore preserves the entire projected group halfspace, not only the original witness. This is a finite-parameter exact cover comparison; it does not rely on an infinitesimal contact surviving automatically. Original nondeep groups remain slack.

The emerging-base repair is valid under the explicitly stated ambient and original-positive-section Hausdorff convergence assumptions. A common bounded base envelope is finite. Sections at all original zero-volume or empty bases have total volume tending to zero by upper containment in neighborhoods of their original sections. Each such integer base is outside the original positive-base hull, so fixed pure-integer separating caps cover these sections with vanishing budgets. Original positive-section convergence is correctly retained as an independent premise; ambient convergence alone cannot replace it.

In a genuinely signed linear variation space, the resulting universal selection condition is equivalent to a finite cover by closed convex protecting cones. The independent-representative criterion and maximal-deficiency proof yield an essential index subset whose entire menu span has dimension at most its size minus one. Thus the common kernel has codimension at most k(I)-1. It does not supply fixed balancing multipliers.

Gaussian cone masses are probabilities in the deformation space only. Their sum is at least one by exact overlap counting. The two-cone classification and the sector sharpness examples are valid. The source correctly forbids applying the linear rank theorem to nonsmooth response functions or to an arbitrary one-sided compatibility cone.

No limit exchanges cap measure with ambient volume, no affine map changes the lattice, and newly appearing mass is expressly included in any derivative. The unproved task is still to extract a below-target descent or an original-measure bound from these structural facts.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
